sections.h2: Cash buyer or listing in Pflugerville
sections.html:
Speed depends on which route you pick. Cash buyers can wrap up in a few weeks; a listing means showings, an inspection and a lender's approval. The city is fifteen miles north of Austin on Farm Road 1825, and shoppers here tend to compare it with Austin and Round Rock.

Expect a lower price from cash, balanced by a closing date of your choosing. A listing can net more, though repairs, staging and a loan contingency come along. Write both outcomes down and compare them.

  • Direct sale suits a deadline, needed repairs, tenants or a lien.
  • A listing suits a sound house and a patient owner.
  • Read every closing cost line before signing.

sections.h2: How Pflugerville's housing came to be
sections.html:
Pflugerville lies in northeastern Travis County, and the town was tiny for most of its life. About 380 people remained in 1949, 662 counted in 1980, and 4,444 by 1990. It then reached 16,335 residents in 2000. No Texas community grew faster between 1980 and 1988.

That history means most houses arrived in waves of new subdivisions, so builder and age tell a buyer more than the street does. Older farmhouses and early town lots near the old center are a different product from tract homes built in the 1980s and after, and buyers price them differently. Say plainly which kind of house you own.

No property tax goes to the state. Your bill is built from local units: county, school district, city. The appraisal district fixes value on January 1, which is also when that year's tax lien attaches.

Texas property tax dates a Pflugerville owner will meet
DateWhat happens
January 1Value set; lien attaches
Near April 1Homestead value notices arrive
May 15Protests generally due
Near October 1Bills go out
February 1Unpaid bills are late, with 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest

A collection fee of up to 20 percent can follow. Homeowners get a $140,000 school exemption. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, get an extra $60,000 and a ceiling on school tax. Homestead appraisals can rise 10% a year at most.

Request a payoff from the Travis County tax office, and the title company will divide this year's bill between you and the buyer. If the notice arrives late, 30 days from delivery can be the later protest date.

After you sign before a notary, the deed goes to the clerk of the county where the land lies. For Pflugerville that is the Travis County Clerk.

Expect $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, along with extra records fees. A warranty deed is the usual form, and the closing statement shows the total.

Not sure which county your parcel is in? Settle that before the deed is drafted, because a deed filed in the wrong county holds up closing.

All three problems here move quickly. Once a default notice arrives, you have 20 days to pay what is overdue and reinstate. A sale notice must come at least 21 days before the auction, which is held on a first Tuesday.

If the auction brings in less than you owe, the lender has two years to sue for the shortfall; any surplus goes to junior lienholders first and then to you. After a death, a will is normally probated within four years, and an estate worth up to $75,000 apart from the homestead may qualify for a small estate affidavit.

  • Late on payments: get the reinstatement figure in writing.
  • Back taxes: ask the collector about an installment plan.
  • Inherited house: decide who may sign before taking an offer.

Being behind on the mortgage does not stop a sale. The payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the servicer can give you the reinstatement amount and sale date.

sections.h2: What to gather before showing the house
sections.html:
Shoppers in a fast-built suburb repeat the same questions, so answer them ahead of time. Begin with paperwork showing what the house is and what has been done to it.

  • The deed and survey, which carry the legal description and any easements.
  • Permits and receipts for additions, roofs, air conditioning and fences.
  • The current tax bill and appraisal notice, plus owners' association dues and rules.
  • Utility bills from one summer and one winter month, which Austin buyers tend to request.

Next, inspect the place the way an inspector would: roof, foundation line, garage door, drainage around the slab, water heater. Hairline foundation cracks and sticking doors get noticed, and a repair estimate in hand is better than a surprise on inspection day.

If you would rather skip that, a direct buyer will typically take the house as is. Make sure the written offer says so, and that no repair requests can be added later without your agreement.

Ask who covers the title policy, how many days closing takes and whether the price can shift after a walkthrough. Request proof of funds and the earnest money amount, and find out under what terms the deposit comes back to you.

Steer clear of anyone who asks for a fee before making an offer or who will not put terms in writing. If the house has a tenant, a lien or heirs who have not agreed, say so in the first conversation. Buyers who learn about a problem late usually respond by trimming the price.

Measure each offer by what lands in your account and when. Take commissions, repairs, carrying costs, concessions and title charges off each price, then line up the results.

Find out if the buyer closes on your date, whether an inspection can kill the deal, who buys the title policy and whether earnest money is required. Where an owners' association covers your street, ask early for its status letter.

After you accept, the title company opens a file, searches for liens, orders the tax figures and sets the signing. Carry photo ID and all the keys. The settlement statement shows price, payoffs, prorated taxes and fees, and once the deed is recorded the rest is yours.

Without a lender's appraisal and underwriting, a cash sale moves fast. Should a lien, a missing heir or a tenant surface, have the buyer write down the new closing date. Do not pay anyone just to get an offer.

faqs.q: Which county records a Pflugerville deed?
faqs.a: Travis County, since Pflugerville is in northeastern Travis County. Ask the title company to confirm your parcel's county before the deed is drafted.

faqs.q: When did Pflugerville start growing quickly?
faqs.a: In the 1980s. No Texas community grew faster from 1980 through 1988, and population reached 16,335 by 2000.

faqs.q: When are Pflugerville property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. Interest and penalty start on February 1, and the penalty keeps rising monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline to protest my Pflugerville appraisal?
faqs.a: Usually May 15, unless the notice arrives late and 30 days from delivery is later. Because the value dates from January 1, it also feeds into the year's tax split at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pflugerville house that is behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. The loan is paid from your proceeds at closing. If a foreclosure notice has gone out, ask the servicer for the reinstatement amount and sale date, which falls on a first Tuesday.
